This section reviews radian measure and the basic trigonometric functions.
Angles are measured in degrees or radians. The number of radians in the central angle

A′CB′ within a circle of radius r is defined as the number of “radius units” contained in the arc s subtended by that central angle. If we denote this central angle by u when mea- sured in radians, this means that u = s>r (Figure 1.36), or

If the circle is a unit circle having radius r = 1, then from Figure 1.36 and Equation (1), we see that the central angle u measured in radians is just the length of the arc that the angle cuts from the unit circle. Since one complete revolution of the unit circle is 360° or
r = 1, u is the length of arc AB that central angle ACB cuts from the unit circle.
